whatItIs.text: Noodles of wheat dough — rolled, cut, or pulled — the everyday noodles of Chinese, Japanese, and Korean cooking, from egg noodles to udon.

historyNote.text: The oldest physical evidence of noodles is a 4,000-year-old bowl from China's Lajia site, and noodles made from wheat dough became a Han-dynasty staple; food historians trace the boiling-dough tradition from China along the Silk Road to Persia and only later to Sicily and Italy.

howToChoose.text: Fresh noodles for texture when cooking same-day, dried for the cupboard; match thickness to broth or stir-fry, and check for a short ingredient list (wheat, water, salt, maybe egg).

storage.text: Dried keeps in a sealed box; fresh noodles are perishable and need the fridge within days. The rulebook has the details.

foodSafetyRef.note: fresh-noodle windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Leftover noodles crisped in a hot pan make noodle cakes; they also thicken soup or turn into chow mein with whatever vegetables you have.
